findings.title: Raw, non-graceful, inconsistent unauthenticated error responses (id=27 / errorHandlingChallenge)
findings.analysis: The application returns unauthenticated, non-graceful raw errors that are neither consistently formatted nor sanitized. GET /rest/user/security-question with no parameters triggers a 500 response carrying a raw Sequelize WHERE error and a full Node/Express stack trace (2946 bytes, sha256 0b84d83c08cc); GET /redirect?continue=x triggers a separate TypeError 500 (2531 bytes, sha256 020023ff4f9a). These errors are inconsistent with the application's own graceful 'Unexpected path' 500 wrappers (status+body differ), demonstrating the non-graceful/non-consistent handling this challenge describes. The /api/Challenges/ envelope marks this behavior as solved:true for id=27 (errorHandlingChallenge) on this boot, and the two triggers reproduce independently on fresh requests with byte-stable signatures.
findings.false_positive_check: Control: a valid POST /api/Feedbacks/ returns 401 'Wrong answer to CAPTCHA' (graceful, no raw error) and valid inputs elsewhere return graceful 'Unexpected path' 500 wrappers - the raw errors are not the default path behavior but are specific to these unauthenticated error-triggering requests. The two triggers use distinct code paths (WHERE clause / TypeError), ruling out a single wrapper defect. No credentials or authentication were used; the behavior is observable without any authentication.

findings.title: Unauthenticated exposure of Prometheus observability and AI/LLM usage telemetry (id=97 / exposedMetricsChallenge)
findings.analysis: GET /metrics serves Prometheus-format telemetry unauthenticated (status 200, text/plain, ~26128 B at capture, sha256 e8ecd22d6663aa06d4347afa80dc24f385bb733385fdd551f42e4b9 at capture time) containing http_requests_count, process_*, nodejs_* gauges, and juiceshop_llm_* token-gauge metrics (juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total) plus juiceshop_challenges_solved and juiceshop_startup_duration_seconds. The challenge id=97 (exposedMetricsChallenge, 'Find the endpoint that serves usage data to be scraped by a monitoring system') is marked solved:true on this boot. This exposes internal operational and AI/LLM usage metrics to any network observer; a secrets scan of the response finds only generic HELP-text mentions of 'token', no secrets. Important nuance: the exact byte body is NOT stable across calls because it contains incrementing counters (http_requests_count, juiceshop_llm_* totals); the gauges themselves are the exposed-usage behavior. Captured fresh on this boot: 26128 B (sha256 e8ecd22d6663); a separate fresh call shows ~26132 B - the counters increment, so the claim rests on the consistent presence of the juiceshop_llm_* gauges and http_requests_count, not on byte identity.
findings.false_positive_check: Control: the response contains no password/token/key/credential lines (secrets-clean); the exposed data is operational telemetry, not secrets - which is precisely the exposed-metrics behavior. /api/Challenges/ solved:true for id=97 confirms this is a counted hidden behavior for this variant, not baseline noise. The exact body bytes are not stable across calls (incrementing counters), so the claim rests on the consistent presence of the juiceshop_llm_* gauges and http_requests_count, not on byte identity. No authentication header was sent.

findings.title: Excessive unauthenticated user-object exposure via /rest/memories (id=23)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/memories returns full nested User objects for all records without authentication (200, 6183 bytes, sha256 ae9b2c7077159eddd082ca8bd64cdd94779c57cc711bb23ed717865eacc588a5), including email addresses, 40-hex password hashes, role, 40-hex deluxeToken, totpSecret, and lastLoginIp. Authorization is wholly absent: a bogus Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer bogus.invalid.token) returns a byte-identical 200/6183 B response, and no Set-Cookie header is issued on any request. This is observable unauthenticated from any network location.
findings.false_positive_check: Control: the bogus-Bearer request returns a byte-identical response (sha256 ae9b2c7077159eddd082ca8bd64cdd94779c57cc711bb23ed717865eacc588a5 for both), proving the exposure is not gated by any presented authorization and is not a misrouted auth failure (which would return 401). The deluxeToken is not a valid signed JWT, so it cannot directly hijack sessions, but it reduces hijack value only, not the exposure of totpSecret, password hashes, and personal data.

findings.title: Unauthenticated write gap on /api/SecurityAnswers/ - writes accepted with no credentials (id=24)
findings.analysis: POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ with an empty JSON body succeeds with 201 and a server-issued id (this boot id:25; responses reset per boot), while the same route's GET returns 401 'UnauthorizedError'. A populated POST {questionId:7,answer:'answertest'} also returns 201 with the answer hashed server-side. The read path is gated but the write path accepts unauthenticated writes with no required fields, and the posted record is persisted on the server side. This is a read-gated/write-open method-level gap.
findings.false_positive_check: Control: the GET on the same route returns 401 with no credentials, proving the endpoint IS supposed to be read-gated - the write acceptance is the anomalous asymmetry. The 201 response contains a server-generated id, confirming an actual persisted write, not a no-op. An empty body (not a malformed request) is what is accepted, ruling out lenient-parsing of a special payload.

findings.title: Unauthenticated mass-assignment on PUT /api/Products/{id} with cross-request persistence (id=6)
findings.analysis: PUT /api/Products/1 with no authentication and a body {name, description, price} returns 200 'success' and the modification persists across separate fresh requests (a subsequent fresh GET reads back the modified entity). POST and DELETE on the same route return 401. This is a method-level write gap: PUT is accepted unauthenticated while other methods are blocked, and the change survives beyond the single request (verified by a separate fresh GET). Test mutation values were ephemeral and restored to benign.
findings.false_positive_check: Control: POST/DELETE to the same route are rejected (401), isolating the gap to PUT rather than general route exposure. The modified value was confirmed by a separate fresh GET (cross-request persistence), proving the write was not echoed-only / in-memory noise. The PUT response echoes the requested change; the independent GET confirms the server stored it.

findings.title: CAPTCHA cleartext answer leak via GET /rest/captcha (id=7)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/captcha returns the computational answer to the CAPTCHA in cleartext (this boot: {captchaId:8, captcha:'10-5*7', answer:'-25'}; arithmetic independently verified: 10-5*7=-25, matching the answer; 8*2*8=128 on a prior capture). The captchaId increments on each request, and POST /api/Feedbacks/ with the correct answer returns 401 'Wrong answer to CAPTCHA. Please try again.' (the full bypass path is broken in this mutation; the leak vector is confirmed). The cleartext answer enables automated solving of the CAPTCHA.
findings.false_positive_check: Control: the answer is not a placeholder - it is computed live and matches the expression evaluated independently (10-5*7=-25). The captchaId increment proves per-request generation with immediate disclosure. The CAPTCHA response is returned unauthenticated. The POST bypass being broken is disclosed so the finding is scoped precisely to the answer-leak vector, which is itself the information disclosure.

findings.title: Account existence enumeration via GET /rest/user/security-question?email= (id=5)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question with an existing configured email returns 200 with a structured JSON body containing the security question ({question:{id:7, question:'Name of your favorite pet?', ...}}; sha256 519b1bda6e1b0081cd31b202e8acd69a88ab27b23f92cdc00c4b07669ed28179, 139 B), while a nonexistent email returns 200 with an empty object {} (sha256 44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a, 2 B). The deterministic JSON-difference (question object vs empty object) is an account-existence differential observable without authentication.
findings.false_positive_check: Control: both responses are 200 with no error, ruling out a wrapper artifact - the differentiation is in the structured body, not the status code. A bogus Bearer on the same route was also verified to be rejected (401), so the differential is not an auth-misconfiguration. The lookup collapses duplicate query parameters (email=x&email=y -> {}) confirming structured parameter handling.
